description: Declarative registry of binary-anchored offset detectors for RS3ProjectXUpdater. Each anchor maps one or more engine offsets (Offsets.kt) to a RELIABLE in-binary code location whose disassembly directly encodes the offset, plus a structural extraction recipe (the `extract` DSL). EXPORT fills sig_blob/sig_mask/feat_hash and resolves old_value against the OLD binary; IMPORT re-resolves against the NEW binary and flags drift (new_value != old_value). `old_value` is hand-seeded from the verified Offsets.kt and acts as a sanity bound. `validated:true` means the recipe was confirmed by hand against a live binary this session; `false` means seed/best-effort, to be confirmed by the export self-test (IMPORT against the source build must reproduce old_value).

steps: find       {match, dst?, src?, mem?:{base,index,scale,disp}, imm?, occurrence?} — scan forward from entry for the Nth matching instruction; sets the cursor
find_after {same as find} — scan forward from the current cursor (after the previous step)
capture    {from:'mem.disp'|'imm', as:VAR} — record a displacement or immediate into VAR (attached to the matched instruction of the preceding find)
rip_target {match, as:VAR} — capture the absolute resolved target of a RIP-relative MOV/LEA
back_scan  {from_call:FUNC, match, mem:{base,...}, capture, occurrence?} — from a CALL to FUNC, scan backwards for a [base+disp] load
call_arg   {call:FUNC, arg:N, capture} — capture disp of `LEA argRegN,[base+disp]` immediately before a CALL to FUNC

dst_reg accepts the ABI-neutral token '@this', resolved to RDI on SysV/ELF and RCX on Win64/PE. NEVER hardcode a register name in a recipe: it silently matches an unrelated instruction on the other platform (a literal "RDI" made OPathingEntity.HITMARKS_AND_HEADBARS resolve to garbage on the PE).
dsl.operands: register placeholders: '@name' binds a register on first use and refers to it after; '*' is wildcard. mem match fields are optional; scale/disp matched only when present.
dsl.emit: value is an integer expression over captured vars and hex/dec consts using + - * << (). One anchor may emit multiple offsets via emit[]. min(a,b) and max(a,b) are also available. Use them when the two platforms emit the same pair of accesses in a different ORDER, so an occurrence-indexed capture cannot be relied on to mean the same field on both.
dsl.manager_class: ALTERNATIVE to anchor/extract: an anchor with {"manager_class":"jag::SomeManager","min_sites":N,"disp_min":"0x400","disp_max":"0x20000"} resolves by CONSENSUS — the tool scans every CALL to a method of that C++ class and reads the preceding `MOV/LEA RDI,[client+OFF]` this-load; the most common OFF (in [disp_min,disp_max], default 0x400-0x20000) wins. This is the most reliable OClient-pointer anchor (many independent callsites agree) and needs no anchor function. CRITICAL: keep disp_min high enough to exclude nested-object this-loads (this=[parent+0x20]) which can otherwise out-count the real client offset. min_sites guards weak consensus. Discover the class->offset map for a new build with `dump managers[:lo-hi]`; find where field-read managers are stored with `dump ctorstores:*@lo-hi`.
dsl.portability: A recipe must resolve on BOTH the ELF and the PE build of the same client. The three things that break portability: (1) hardcoded registers - use '@this'; (2) absolute disp_min/disp_max windows tuned to one build's struct layout - the same struct can sit at a different offset on the other ABI, and a window that is correct for one can select the WRONG field on the other; (3) occurrence-indexed captures where the compilers order the accesses differently - disambiguate with min()/max() or a semantic delta instead.
dsl.matcher_limits: A recipe MUST bound every capture with disp_min/disp_max. The matcher does NOT honour mem.index, mem.scale or a top-level imm key: a step that relies on any of them silently matches the first instruction of that mnemonic instead of failing, and the anchor then emits a plausible looking wrong number. Proven on 949-5, where every anchor written that way mis-resolved on both hosts (ONPC.CURRENT_HP.msvc emitted 0x10, OHintTrail.POINT_FINE_HEIGHT 0x30 against a true 0xc, OHintTrailList.SLOT_ARRAY 0x8 against a true 0x10) while every anchor written with base plus a displacement window resolved exactly. A window that excludes the wrong answer turns a lie into an UNRESOLVED, which is the only acceptable failure mode. The underlying reason is that the matcher only understands a simple [base + disp] operand: it cannot constrain, and cannot read a displacement out of, an operand that also carries an index and a scale. So an offset that only ever appears inside a SIB-addressed access - MSVC folds an array index into the load where gcc hoists it into a separate LEA - cannot be anchored at all on that host and belongs in verified_fields.

ofunctions_note: OFunctions consts -> qualified function name. IMPORT resolves each via the function sig-match (functions.ndjson) and emits the full OFunctions block into offsets_<ver>.kt. These are absolute function addresses (they move every build), so no drift flag. Entries that exist on only one host (the MSVC-only Windows input-source pair) resolve there and report an ofunction failure on the other, which is the same self-selecting behaviour the .msvc anchors use.

jag::graphics::WorldToScreen (949-1 @0xa6e2b0) projects a world-space AABB to screen; its matrix args are (out, arg2=viewMatrix, arg3=scaleMatrix, arg4=projectionMatrix). Callers (e.g. the entity-projection helper @0x3ca1a0) issue `LEA RSI,[World+VIEW]; LEA RDX,[World+SCALE]; LEA RCX,[World+PROJECTION]` directly before the CALL, so call_arg arg2 => VIEW_MATRIX and call_arg arg4 => PROJECTION_MATRIX. CRITICAL: PROJECTION is arg4 (the combined view*proj @0x13200 that WorldToScreen actually samples for screen x/y), NOT arg3 (the middle SCALE matrix @0x13180 that the old Mat4x4Multiply-caller recipe wrongly emitted as projection). via_caller picks the first caller whose args are BOTH direct LEAs; callers that pass projection via a register alias (MOV RCX,R14) fail call_arg and are skipped automatically.

Emitted by the WorldToScreen anchor as call_arg arg4 (the combined view*proj matrix WorldToScreen samples). 949-1 = 0x13200 (VIEW 0x13100 + 0x100). Re-seeded from the stale 948-5 0x131e0; 0x13180 is the middle SCALE matrix, NOT projection.

MSVC counterpart of OWorld.VIEW_MATRIX. On Windows jag::graphics::WorldToScreen is INLINED, so that anchor's call_arg recipe has no CALL to hang off and reports anchor-not-located - which silently carried the stale Linux values forward and broke every world-space overlay. MSVC vectorises the projection into MULPS reads of the combined view*proj rows at proj+0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30, while the view matrix is read with scalar MULSS/ADDSS - so MULPS alone selects the projection matrix inside this function. occurrence 1 is proj+0x10 in 949-4; VIEW is a fixed 0x100 below PROJECTION (SCALE sits between them at +0x80). Beware: an interleaved second triple holds the INVERSES of all three and yields a negative clipW, so a wrong pick reads as 'everything is off screen' rather than as garbage. This anchor is self-selecting: it fails on the gcc build (no jag::game::DrawEntityHitmarks) exactly as the WorldToScreen anchor fails on MSVC.

Callers reach the embedded HeightMap subobject as `<this> = World + HEIGHT_MAP` before CALL GetFineHeight. This uses back_scan rather than call_arg because the two compilers emit that address computation differently: the ELF build emits `LEA arg1,[World+disp]` but the PE build emits `ADD RCX,disp` on a register that already holds the World. call_arg only matches LEA, so it silently found nothing on the PE; back_scan's this-load reader handles LEA, MOV and ADD/SUB-immediate alike. dst_reg is '@this' so the register is resolved per ABI.

jag::game::World::GetMapSquare is the world->mapsquare index accessor. Both builds subtract the two origin fields from the arguments and then load the mapsquares vector (outer stride 0x18), but they do it in OPPOSITE order: the ELF build subtracts Y first, the PE build subtracts X first. The old occurrence-indexed recipe therefore assigned X and Y the wrong way round on the PE. X_OFFSET is always the lower of the two displacements on both builds, so the pair is disambiguated with min()/max() instead of by order. X_MAX and Y_MAX are derived: the four build-area bounds are contiguous dwords in the order X_OFFSET, Y_OFFSET, X_MAX, Y_MAX on both builds (verified independently against the World constructor's argument stores and against the double-loop scene walker on each). MAPSQUARES_VECTOR is captured independently as the first 64-bit load after the two subtractions. The disp window is deliberately wide enough to span both layouts, which is safe because the recipe runs inside GetMapSquare, whose only struct accesses are these.
Emitted by the World::GetMapSquare anchor (see OWorld.MAPSQUARE_X_OFFSET).
Emitted by the World::GetMapSquare anchor (see OWorld.MAPSQUARE_X_OFFSET). Outer 2D vector triple, stride 0x18 outer / 0x8 inner.

The World ctor jag::game::World::World (949-1 @0x4c4620) constructs a graphics::GraphNode and stores it at World+ROOT_GRAPH_NODE (`MOV [World+0x10170], graphNodePtr`, param_1[0x202e]). The window 0x10169-0x1017f isolates the root ptr from the AABB float area just below it (0x10130-0x10168; the old 948-5 root offset 0x10150 now lives inside that AABB) and the SSE zero-init at 0x10180 above it. occ1 MOV-mem in that window = 0x10170. Window is tight by necessity (root is 0x8 above the AABB); a larger future drift reports UNRESOLVED, which is still a drift signal.

MSVC counterpart of OWorld.ROOT_GRAPH_NODE. gcc stores the GraphNode inline in the World ctor (MOV [World+ROOT_GRAPH_NODE]), so the gcc anchor finds it by a tight disp window on that store. MSVC outlines construct-and-store into a helper that receives the AABB block base and writes to param+0x40, so no disp32 for ROOT_GRAPH_NODE exists in the ctor at all and the gcc recipe reports 'step find no match'. What MSVC does emit is LEA <reg>,[World+AABB_BASE] to pass that base to the helper; the root pointer is a fixed 0x40 above it. Window is tight by the same necessity as the gcc anchor: a larger future drift reports UNRESOLVED, which is still a drift signal.

GetLocationContainerAt reads `CMP qword [ms+0x70],0` to select chunkSize 16 vs 8. First such compare in the function. LINUX-CONFIRMED (949-4): GetLocationContainerAt@0x4991a0 computes chunkSize = (*(long*)(this+0x70)==0) ? 16 : 8 via the `(-(uint)(x==0) & 8) + 8` idiom, so CHUNK_SIZE_FLAG and COMPOSITE_DATA are the SAME field at +0x70.

Same accessor as OMapSquare.CHUNK_SIZE_FLAG. GetLocationContainerAt (949-1 @0x4991a0) reads the location-container 2D vector base as its FIRST instruction `MOV R8,[MapSquare+0xeb80]` (then +0xeb88 = vector end). occ1 MOV-mem in window 0xe800-0xf000 = 0xeb80. +0x18 vs 948-5 (0xeb68). HitmarksAndHeadbars is a POINTER field on PathingEntity; the caller does `MOV <this>,[entity+HMH]` immediately before CALL AddHeadbar. dst_reg is '@this' rather than a literal register - the previous literal "RDI" matched an unrelated RDI write on the PE and produced the nonsense value 0xffffffffffffff98, which shipped in the Windows offset table. The disp window rejects stack spills so the scan walks past them. (The call is deep inside the large ProcessExtendedInfo functions - needs RECIPE_MAX_INSNS >= ~4000.)

MANAGER_CLASS anchor — consensus over every callsite of a jag::NPCList method: each loads `MOV/LEA RDI,[client+0x194b8]` (the this-arg) before the CALL. 17/17 sites agree. This is the most reliable manager-offset anchor available.

MANAGER_CLASS anchor — callsites of jag::ConnectionManager methods load `RDI,[client+0x19440]`. min_sites lowered 10->2 for 949-1: only ~6-7 CM methods are named in this build (vs many in 948-5), and most intra-CM calls pass `this` in a register, so the agreeing this-load count is small (~2-3 clean sites at 0x19440). One outlier at 0x194a8 comes from LoginProtocolHandler (operates on MainLogicManager, client+0x194a8); 0x19440 still wins by count. Naming more CM methods in future builds will raise the margin.

jag::ProjectileList::Add opens by loading the Client from the list's back-pointer and then the SceneManager out of it, on both hosts: ELF `MOV R9,[list+0x8]; MOV RDI,[R9+SCENE_MANAGER]` and PE `MOV RAX,[list+0x8]; MOV RCX,[RAX+SCENE_MANAGER]`, each the first Client-sized displacement in the function. Replaces a manager_class consensus over jag::game::SceneManager, which was unbeatable on the ELF (37/37 sites) but abstained on the PE, where that class has no named methods for the consensus to walk - the anchor now resolves on BOTH hosts. The window starts at 0x18000 rather than 0x10000 so the World's ROOT_GRAPH_NODE load a few instructions later, which sits in the same broad range on both builds, can never be picked instead.

MANAGER_CLASS anchor — 18/26 callsites of jag::InterfaceManager methods load `RDI,[client+0x19488]`. (Field is named INTERFACE_LIST in Offsets.kt; the C++ class is InterfaceManager.) min_sites lowered 5->3: the PE build has far fewer InterfaceManager methods named, and requiring 5 distinct callsites made the consensus abstain on a class whose offset every callsite agrees on.

MANAGER_CLASS anchor — 5-7 callsites of jag::game::Camera methods load `RDI,[client+0x19420]`. MANAGER_CLASS anchor — the two TelemetryGrid callsites of jag::game::WorldList::InsertOrReplace (949-1 @0x6c1f30) load `RDI,[client+0x193d8]` (zero disagreement). Depends on WorldList::InsertOrReplace being named in the build; if the manager class has no named methods the consensus fails (as it did before this re-baseline). Low site count (2) — MEDIUM confidence.

UpdateStat reaches its table by walking Client -> MainLogicManager -> StatTable, and both compilers emit that walk as two consecutive qword loads: ELF `MOV RSI,[RDI]; MOV RDI,[RSI+MAINLOGIC_MANAGER]; MOV R9,[RDI+STAT_TABLE]`, PE `MOV RAX,[this+0x8]; MOV RCX,[RAX+MAINLOGIC_MANAGER]; MOV RDI,[RCX+STAT_TABLE]`. Step 1's window is the Client-field region and step 2's is the MainLogicManager-field region, so the two cannot swap. StatTable and ClientVarDomain are adjacent member pointers on the manager - 0x73a0/0x73a8 on the ELF, 0x7618/0x7620 on the PE - so the third emit derives the domain from the table. Replaces an anchor on jag::ConnectionManager::LoginProtocolHandler that carried no symbol on the PE and reported anchor-not-located there; UpdateStat is in the OFunctions set, so it is named on every build of both hosts by construction.
Emitted by the LoginProtocolHandler anchor (see OMainLogicManager.STAT_TABLE). ClientVarDomain = StatTable + 8.

Every caller of jag::ProjectileList::Add loads the list as `MOV <this>,[client+PROJECTILE_LIST]` before the call. jag::ProjectileList::Add is in the OFunctions set so it is guaranteed to be named on both builds, which makes this a portable substitute for a manager_class consensus (there is only one named ProjectileList method, so consensus would abstain). The disp window keeps the scan from latching onto a nested-object this-load or a stack spill.

Anchored on ReadTileFlags rather than on the HasBridgeFlag wrapper: HasBridgeFlag exists as a real function on both builds, but MSVC ALSO inlines it at ~20 sites, so anchoring there samples an unrepresentative subset of callers. ReadTileFlags is the common leaf both wrappers funnel into. back_scan (not call_arg) for the same reason as OWorld.HEIGHT_MAP: the PE computes the subobject address with `ADD RCX,disp`, which call_arg's LEA-only scan misses. Cross-check: LINK_MAP sits exactly 0x10 above HEIGHT_MAP on both builds.

MSVC counterpart. The gcc manager_class recipe cannot fire on the PE (jag::game::Camera had no named methods there). Anchored on the newly-named CS2 opcode handler. Step 1 is a POSITIONING step only - it steps the cursor past the LOGGED_IN_PLAYER guard so that a future codegen change turning that guard from CMP into MOV+TEST cannot make step 2 capture the guard's displacement instead. Deliberately does NOT emit LOGGED_IN_PLAYER: that field already has a hand-verified value and anchors are applied after verified fields, so emitting it could only overwrite something good. Neither step hardcodes a register and step 2 consumes nothing bound by step 1 - only the cursor carries - so the cross-step register-binding failure that killed three earlier recipes cannot occur. The disp window bounds captures to the Client-field region so a stack spill can never be emitted.

949-5 @0x00188880: `MOV R9,[@this]` loads the Client, then `MOV RDI,[R9+0x19480]` loads the HintTrailList. It is the only client-struct-sized displacement in the function, so the first 64-bit [reg+disp] load in the 0x10000..0x20000 window is it. NOT YET VALIDATED by an EXPORT run against the previous build - do that before trusting it on update day. CROSS-CHECKED ON THE PE at 949-5: the handler there reaches the list twice, `ADD RCX,0x198b8` on the set path and `MOV RCX,[RCX+0x198b8]` @0x00107a8e on the clear path. Only the latter is a memory operand, so this recipe resolves on both hosts (PE old_value 0x198b8).

BOTH HOSTS, one recipe. ELF 949-5 @0x00185fc3 `MOV RBP,[RSI+0x19478]`; PE 949-5 @0x000f91b2 `MOV RDI,[RAX+0x198b0]` (old_value there is 0x198b0). Each function's other [reg+disp] loads are small frame/vtable offsets, so the 0x10000..0x20000 window isolates the client-struct field on both. Distinct from OClient.HINTTRAIL_LIST, which is the NEXT pointer along (+8) and a different subsystem. NOT YET VALIDATED by an EXPORT run against the previous build.

The AnimationWrapper's frame cursor: the value the wrapper last emitted per-frame events up to, compared each tick against the playback state's frame counter at [[wrapper+0x18]+0x98]. gcc inlines the whole frame-event loop into AnimationWrapper::Update, which copies `this` into a callee-saved register in the prologue and then reads the cursor with a 32-bit load through it. The wrapper has no other member between 0x20 and 0x30 - 0x28 is a std::function reached by LEA - and a byte scan of the function finds a single 32-bit load at any displacement in that range, so the first one is the cursor. An earlier recipe tried to bind the callee-saved register off the `MOV reg,<this-reg>` in the prologue; the matcher does not resolve a register token in the source position, so that step never fired. Self-selecting: MSVC splits the loop out into its own function, so this anchor's name resolves only on the ELF and the PE is served by OAnimation.CURRENT_FRAME.msvc. OAnimation.ID is the wrapper's first member and carries no displacement to capture, so it is supplied by verified_fields on both platforms.

MSVC counterpart of OAnimation.CURRENT_FRAME. MSVC keeps the frame-event loop out of line as jag::game::AnimationWrapper::EmitFrameEvents, which opens by loading the playback state from [this+0x18] and then reading the frame cursor with `MOV ESI,[this+0x24]` (949-5 @0x2f0df2) - the first 32-bit read through the this-register, and the only wrapper member between 0x20 and 0x30. The function ends by storing the state's new counter back to the same slot on every return path. Self-selecting: gcc inlines this loop into AnimationWrapper::Update, so the name resolves only on the PE. This is the anchor that was missing when the PE table shipped no OAnimation at all and every scripted read of an entity's animation threw OffsetUnavailableException on Windows.

MSVC counterpart of OClient.INTERFACE_LIST. The gcc anchor is a manager_class consensus over jag::InterfaceManager, which abstains on the PE because too few of that class's methods carry names there for the required agreeing-site count. DoOpComponentInner loads the manager from the Client three times, once per path, and hands it to InterfaceManager::IfButtonXInner as `this`; the first of those loads is also the first Client-sized displacement in the function. Self-selecting: the ELF's only caller of IfButtonXInner is IfButtonX, and this MiniMenu inner handler carries no symbol there, so the recipe cannot fire on the wrong host. Also emits OClient.INPUT_EVENT_VIEW, which is the same Client field: the interface manager is what carries the tick's copied input-event vectors, and jag::ClientProt::FlushPerTick reaches the key-event vector through this very displacement.

MSVC counterpart of OClient.BUILD_AREA_VECTOR. The gcc anchor is a manager_class consensus over jag::game::WorldList that depends on WorldList::InsertOrReplace being named - true on the ELF via its TelemetryGrid callers, false on the PE, where the consensus abstains. The multi-scene rebuild handler opens `MOV RAX,[this]; MOV R14,[RAX+BUILD_AREA_VECTOR]` and then clears and refills the vector at its 0x68 element stride, so the first Client-sized displacement in the function is the vector. Self-selecting: the handler carries no symbol on the ELF.

The key-down map is a pair of adjacent globals - the tree root and, 0x10 below it, the end sentinel the walk compares its candidate against - and the two are always touched together at the top of the lookup: the root is loaded RIP-relative and the sentinel is taken with a RIP-relative LEA on the very next instruction. Both are absolute addresses, so they move on every build and must be anchored rather than carried. IsKeyDown is the whole lookup and opens with exactly that pair, so occurrence 1 of each is unambiguous. Self-selecting: MSVC inlines IsKeyDown at every call site and the PE has no standalone copy to name, which is why the PE is served by the .msvc variant on SetKeyDown instead - and why OFunctions.INPUTSTATE_ISKEYDOWN is withheld there. The same recipe also pins the node: the first 32-bit CMP through a node after the globals are taken is the key comparison that drives the descent, and the pressed byte is the next slot up on both hosts - the ELF returns it as the function's result and the PE stores 1 into it. The two child words at +0x0 and +0x8 carry no displacement to capture and are recorded as verified fields instead.

The monotonic clock the client stamps input samples with and both mouse prot senders delta-encode against. It is an absolute .data address, so it moves on every build. The movement producer loads it RIP-relative and stores it verbatim into the sample's timestamp field, and it is the only global that producer touches. Anchored on the game-event movement delegate, which exists as a named recorder method only on the ELF. Self-selecting: the PE's producer is a different function on a different event stream - jag::ClientProt::RecordNativeMouseMove, which also receives the Win32 message id and a source-flags word - and is served by the .msvc variant.

The movement producer loads it RIP-relative and stores it verbatim into the sample's timestamp field, and it is the only global that producer touches. MSVC counterpart. RecordNativeMouseMove is reached only as a bound callback from a listener table - it has exactly one reference in the image and that reference is data - so it cannot be found by call graph, only by name. It touches no other global.

The MainLogicManager carries TWO rings of identical 0x28 MouseSample entries back to back: the click ring of 50 slots and, immediately after it, the movement ring of 200. Only the movement ring is anchored here; the click ring's fields sit below it and are recorded as verified fields. PopEventMouseMoveSample is the whole pop: it walks Client -> MainLogicManager, compares the two cursors, forms the slot address and advances the read cursor. The write cursor is the dword immediately below the read cursor on both hosts. gcc keeps every displacement manager-relative, so the read cursor is the first 32-bit load through the manager and step 1 only positions the cursor past the Client walk. The slot base is derived rather than captured: the write cursor is the dword immediately after the last slot, so base = write - capacity*stride, and both of those are structural constants recorded as verified fields (200 slots of 0x28). Capturing it directly was tried and abandoned - the matcher does not apply a displacement window to a LEA's address operand, so the step returned a displacement from elsewhere in the function rather than failing, which is worse than not trying. Self-selecting against the .msvc variant: MSVC rebases the manager pointer with an ADD first, so none of these displacements are readable there. The read-cursor window starts at 0x4000 rather than 0x1000 so this recipe cannot fire on the PE: MSVC's rebased cursor displacement is well below that, and before the window was tightened this anchor resolved on the PE too and emitted the rebase-relative numbers, which the later .msvc pass then had to overwrite. An anchor that depends on being corrected afterwards is one reordering away from shipping garbage.

verified_fields._doc: Struct fields established by hand against a specific build, for values no anchor recipe can derive. Emitted BEFORE anchors and OFunctions so anything the tooling can re-derive from the binary wins. Each row records the build it was verified against; on a later build the value is still emitted (dropping it would silently disable engine features) but is downgraded to STALE_CARRY and flagged needs_reverification, so it surfaces as work to redo rather than as a trusted number. common.evidence: Shipped 0xe is the PARENT LAYER COMPONENT ID, not a type. jag::opcode::_if_getlayer returns (interfaceId<<16)|comp[+0xe] with 0xffff meaning no parent layer, and jag::InterfaceManager::GetParentLayer indexes the interface's static component array with it. parked_anchors.notes:
PARKED - deliberately NOT in the executing anchors list; the four OMapSquare values are supplied by verified_fields instead. Kept verbatim so a future session can revive it once the recipe matcher can discriminate operand width on a STORE.
Layout is settled and identical on both 949-4 builds: the constructor writes mapsquareX and mapsquareY as two adjacent dwords, then the ClientCompositeData shared_ptr as {control block, object} in the next two qwords, with the strong count incremented through the control block - which is what makes COUNTER the lower qword and DATA the upper. The four emitted offsets are therefore x, x+4, x+0xc, x+0x14.
WHY IT CANNOT RUN TODAY: the capture wants the first dword store to the object in a small window, but the window is bracketed by a byte store and a qword store to neighbouring offsets, and operandSizeMatches resolves width from the WRITTEN REGISTER - which is null for a store, so it abstains and the recipe captures whichever neighbour comes first. Measured on the ELF: with the window opened wide it captured the constructor's own argument spill (a stack slot, base RSP) and emitted a plausible-looking but wrong quad; narrowed past the spill it captured the byte store instead. Two attempted matcher fixes - rejecting stack-based operands, and reading the x86 size prefix off the memory operand - were both reverted rather than shipped half-working, because operandSizeMatches is shared by every other recipe in this file and a regression there is far more expensive than one parked anchor. A correct revival needs operand width taken from the instruction's memory operand (verified against a store, not just a register write), after which this recipe with a stack-excluding base resolves to the right dword on both the ELF and the PE.
REPLACES A KNOWN-BAD SET: the shipping tables carried a different quad for these four on BOTH platforms; those values are not these fields (one is an unrelated qword sentinel whose value is never tested, one has no MapSquare-relative use at all, and two fall inside the embedded polymorphic subobject). The giveaway was that CHUNK_SIZE_FLAG and COMPOSITE_DATA are the same field yet the table gave them different offsets.

VALIDATED (windowed): animationId is a plain int32 at entity+0xa88 (-1 = none), accessed polymorphically across the binary (NOT set in the small base Entity::Entity @0x13f310). jag::NPCList::ProcessNpcInfo has a single `CMP reg,dword[npc+0xa88]` (the per-tick animation check). The disp window 0xa00-0xb00 isolates it from other field reads. This anchor CONFIRMS the value and DETECTS drift within the window; if animationId moves outside 0xa00-0xb00 the recipe reports UNRESOLVED (still a drift signal). The -1 writer is FUN_00464850 `MOV dword[entity+0xa88],0xffffffff`.
parked_anchors.parked_reason: DISPROVED at 949-4. The recipe is a heuristic range scan - first CMP in jag::NPCList::ProcessNpcInfo with any memory displacement in [0xa00,0xb00] - and it lands on 0xa88, which is slot+0x0 of the second animation slot. FUN_002f07a0 initialises that word with its literal `kind` argument (0 or 1), so it is a slot discriminator and never -1; the engine's `animationId != -1` test could never be false. Real animation ids are the eastl::fixed_vector<int,4> at entity+0x2c8, now emitted as OEntity.ANIM_IDS_BEGIN/ANIM_IDS_END from verified_fields. OEntity.ANIMATION_ID is in withheld_fields; this anchor had to be parked because anchors emit AFTER the withheld filter and were silently re-deriving 0xa88 on Linux.

_parked_anchors_doc: Anchor recipes whose target layout is understood but which the recipe matcher cannot currently express safely. They are NOT executed. Their values live in verified_fields, so the table stays correct while the recipe waits for the matcher capability it needs. Move an entry back into 'anchors' only after proving it resolves to the right value on BOTH platform builds.

recipe_attempts_rejected._doc: Anchor recipes drafted and REJECTED because EXPORT self-validation against the old build did not reproduce the known value. Recorded so the next attempt starts from what already failed instead of re-deriving it. An anchor that resolves to a WRONG value is worse than none: anchors are emitted after verified_fields, so a bad recipe silently overwrites a correct hand-verified offset.
